=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:lines 1503, 1499 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The unresolved-commit-directory reason is added to `unverified_destinations` instead of `unknown_destination_reasons`, grouping it under a push-facing label.
  WHY: Both paths still prompt for confirmation, so the behavior is unchanged and the difference is cosmetic.
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:Summary (line ~4) "A person is needed only when an LLM has failed three distinct times" vs P3 step 2 (~line 269) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: P3 applies `ai:needs-human` to non-plan/non-clarify phases after two consecutive identical fingerprint matches, which conflicts with the summary's three-distinct-failures promise.
  WHY: P6's wording about skipping judge rounds for parked items leaves it ambiguous whether these items get the promised three rounds.
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:P6 | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The plan accepts that a process crash or explicit or ambiguous send failure can lose the Telegram alert while allowing at most one send attempt.
  WHY: This does not guarantee delivery of the CRITICAL Telegram alert; the source does not state a severity.
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:Summary (line ~4) "triggers one CRITICAL Telegram alert" vs P6 step 2 (~line 321) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The summary implies a delivered CRITICAL Telegram alert, while P6 permits the alert to be lost after recording the attempt.
  WHY: The persisted marker prevents retries after success, explicit failure, or ambiguous response, so the summary overstates the delivery guarantee.
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:P6 steps 2–3, lines 315–320 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Re-triggering a parked item resets the round count but does not specify clearing `alert_attempted_at` or `alert_confirmed`.
  WHY: If the marker persists, the at-most-once invariant suppresses a Telegram attempt for a later escalation cycle; if it is cleared, the plan must specify how that interacts with the invariant.
- changelog.d/37432054768-merge-guard-env-chdir.md:filename "37432054768-merge-guard-env-chdir.md" | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The filename uses a GitHub Actions run ID rather than the required issue-or-PR number.
  WHY: It violates the changelog filename convention and needs the owning PR number to be known before renaming.
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:"## Decisions (operator answers, 2026-10-06)" table format (~line 158) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The decisions section uses a qualified heading and table rather than the documented `## Decisions` and `### D<n> — <title>` record format.
  WHY: The fail-open linter treats malformed records as warnings, but the format diverges from the documented convention and is harder for tooling to parse.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: “A person is needed only when an LLM has failed three distinct times.”
  expected_change_site: docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md, P3 failure-signature threshold and P6 escalation policy
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: P3 applies `ai:needs-human` after two repeated signatures for non-plan/non-clarify phases; P3's test says escalation occurs on the “2nd repeat”; P6 says parked `ai:needs-human` items skip new judge rounds; the plan does not define a consistent threshold ensuring the third distinct failure occurs before parking.
- requirement: The PR description says the item “triggers one Telegram alert”; the plan summary likewise promises “one CRITICAL Telegram alert.”
  expected_change_site: P6 alert handling in docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: P6 persists `alert_attempted_at` before sending and forbids any subsequent send after that marker exists, including after explicit or ambiguous failures; the risk section allows a crash after recording the marker to leave the alert unsent, with no retry.
- requirement: G6 and the re-trigger paragraph at P6 line 315 state that a parked item becomes eligible again on a new trigger; the plan does not explicitly say whether `alert_attempted_at` and `alert_confirmed` are cleared with the parked state on re-trigger.
  expected_change_site: docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md, P6 step 2 re-trigger paragraph (line 315)
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: Line 315 specifies removing `ai:needs-human`, clearing the parked state, and resetting the round count, but does not specify what happens to `alert_attempted_at` or `alert_confirmed`; line 317 says never to call Telegram again once the marker exists.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:lines 1503, 1499 | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The changed condition adds the unresolved-commit-directory reason to `unverified_destinations` rather than `unknown_destination_reasons`.
  WHY: Both paths result in a confirmation ask; the combined message groups a commit-directory concern under a push-facing label, but the user-visible prompt still asks for confirmation before the operation runs.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "A person is needed only when an LLM has failed three distinct times." (plan summary, line 4), and G6: "Every human-only stop gets UNBLOCK_MAX_ROUNDS_PER_ITEM (default 3) distinct LLM rounds."
  Expected change site: docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md, P3 failure-signature handling at line 269
  Evidence of absence: P3 line 269 states that for phases other than plan or clarify, `ai:needs-human` is applied after `STALL_FINGERPRINT_REPEAT_MAX` (default 2) consecutive identical fingerprint matches. P6 line 314 states `ai:needs-human` items skip new judge rounds. For non-plan/non-clarify phases, the P3-to-P6 path therefore applies a direct human latch with zero distinct LLM rounds, contradicting G6's requirement of 3 unblock-judge rounds per human stop. The plan should either give those items unblock-judge rounds, note an explicit exception to G6 for fingerprint-breaker escalations, or state that the 2 fingerprint failures plus the unblock judge's assessment count as the 3 distinct rounds even when the label is applied directly.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The plan summary at line 4 says "triggers one CRITICAL Telegram alert." G6 at line 68 says "makes one persisted CRITICAL Telegram send attempt." P6 at line 317 says "Once the marker exists, never call Telegram for that item again, regardless of whether the response is success, explicit failure or ambiguous." The risks section at line 429 says "P6 may lose an alert after recording the attempt."
  Expected change site: docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md, summary line 4
  Evidence of absence: Line 4 uses "triggers one CRITICAL Telegram alert" which implies guaranteed delivery. G6 at line 68 correctly uses "makes one persisted CRITICAL Telegram send attempt" (matching the LAST RUN DIFF refinement), as do the P6 implementation steps and the accepted risk. The summary wording on its own, read before the detailed goals, implies a stronger delivery guarantee than the plan actually provides. The wording discrepancy is minor but G6 is authoritative.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: G6 and the re-trigger paragraph at P6 line 315 state that a parked item becomes eligible again on a new trigger. The plan does not explicitly say whether `alert_attempted_at` and `alert_confirmed` are cleared with the parked state on re-trigger.
  Expected change site: docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md, P6 step 2 re-trigger paragraph (line 315)
  Evidence of absence: Line 315 says "remove `ai:needs-human` before clearing the parked state and resetting the round count to 0." The parked state and the alert ledger fields (`alert_attempted_at`, `alert_confirmed`) share the same ledger entry. Whether "clearing the parked state" means clearing only the parking flag or resetting the entire ledger entry (including alert fields) is not specified. If alert fields persist, a re-triggered item that exhausts its new rounds would digest but never send a fresh alert; if they are cleared, the at-most-once contract from line 317 would need an explicit override for re-trigger scenarios. The implementer must guess.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:P6 step 2 | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The plan persists `alert_attempted_at` across escalation cycles.
  WHY: If the intention is to guarantee an alert for every distinct escalation cycle (as implied by the plan's summary), persisting `alert_attempted_at` across re-triggers will prevent subsequent cycles from attempting to send an alert if the first cycle's attempt (even if unsuccessful) persists.
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:P6 | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The plan states it accepts process crashes as "lost alerts" and guarantees "at most one send attempt".
  WHY: If the requirement is to guarantee delivery of a CRITICAL Telegram alert, the plan fails this because it does not attempt to retry or verify delivery upon an explicit or ambiguous failure.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: “A person is needed only when an LLM has failed three distinct times.”
  Expected change site: docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md, P3 failure-signature handling and P6 escalation policy.
  Evidence of absence: P3 line 269 applies `ai:needs-human` after two repeated signatures for phases other than plan or clarify, which contradicts the "three distinct times" requirement stated in the summary.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:Summary (line ~4) "A person is needed only when an LLM has failed three distinct times" vs P3 step 2 (~line 269) | confidence=[4] | severity=MAJOR
  PROBLEM: The summary and G6 promise three distinct LLM rounds before human escalation, but P3 escalates to `ai:needs-human` directly for non-plan/clarify phases after only 2 same-fingerprint repeats. P6 step 2 (~line 314) says "`ai:needs-human` is itself in `BLOCK_LABELS`: skip new judge rounds for parked items" — the phrase "parked items" is ambiguous between (a) items past the unblock judge's rounds and (b) any item carrying the `ai:needs-human` label. P3 claims all three labels including `ai:needs-human` are in BLOCK_LABELS routed to the unblock judge, but P6 wording suggests freshly-labeled items may skip the unblock judge entirely.
  WHY: An implementer following the plan could either skip the unblock judge for non-plan/clarify phases (contradicting the summary's "three distinct times") or route them through it (which P6 wording is ambiguous about). Either interpretation breaks the documented guarantee for those phases.
